key_insight: The paper shows that ZX-diagrams can directly yield efficient bounds on both entanglement entropy and magic by separating a graph-state backbone from non-Clifford Pauli gadgets.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers and simulation tool builders a scalable way to estimate key resource costs without expensive full tensor contractions.
method: Use ZX-calculus flow to extract a normal form of the diagram.
Treat the normal form as a graph-state backbone plus non-Clifford Pauli gadgets.
Compute additive upper/lower entanglement bounds and an upper bound on logarithmic stabilizer extent, with preprocessing to merge or remove redundant gadgets.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmark the method on random unitary circuits, monitored circuits, and Trotterized Hamiltonian evolution with Clifford layers, reporting informative bounds even at large qubit counts, depths, and spider counts.
watch_item: The bounds are informative rather than exact, so their usefulness depends on how well the ZX normal form captures the circuit structure and on the quality of preprocessing.
paper_title: Entanglement entropy and magic of ZX-diagrams
